content.title: About
content.content: Stewed skinless chicken is tender poultry meat cooked slowly in liquid. This method retains most nutrients while the lack of skin reduces saturated fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken is the most widely consumed meat worldwide.
Stewing keeps the meat juicy even without the skin.
Chicken meat is rich in protein, B‑vitamins, and minerals such as phosphorus and selenium.
Stewed chicken is a staple in many cuisines, from Russian soups to Asian curries.
When stored properly in the refrigerator, cooked stewed chicken lasts 3‑4 days.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken provides all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Removing the skin dramatically cuts saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6) aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals for bone health and immunity
items.content: Phosphorus and selenium support strong bones and act as antioxidants.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: Protein and modest fat help keep you feeling full longer, aiding appetite control.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; ensure proper cooking temperatures.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: Stewed chicken is often seasoned with salt; monitor intake if you need to limit sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skinless stewed chicken can be added to salads, soups, stews, sandwiches, and pasta dishes. It’s easy to dice or shred for vegetable mixes or use as a filling for wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked stewed chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Seafood Thermidor is a dish made from boiled seafood (shrimp, mussels, squid) in a creamy egg‑mustard sauce with cheese and spices, baked until golden. It is traditionally served in individual ramekins and is a staple of upscale cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thermidor originated in France in the late 19th century as a way to serve meat in a sauce, later adapted for seafood.
The creamy Thermidor sauce contains egg yolks that create a characteristic velvety texture when baked.
The dish is often garnished with fresh herbs, lemon wedges, and grated Parmesan.
The original recipe used cognac or brandy, giving the sauce a subtle aromatic note.
Thermidor is frequently presented in small ceramic ramekins to retain heat.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Shrimp, mussels and squid provide high‑quality marine protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood is abundant in EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies zinc, selenium and iodine, important for immune function and thyroid health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Seafood contains vitamin B12 and niacin, aiding energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: The creamy sauce with mustard and cheese provides vitamins A and D, helping combat free radicals.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels or squid.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: The cream sauce and cheese can raise cholesterol levels, so people with hypercholesterolemia should limit portions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauce often contains added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should reduce it.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly handled seafood may contain bacteria or toxins, so use fresh ingredients and cook thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, usually in small ramekins. It can be enjoyed on its own or paired with a light salad, rice, or fresh bread. Before serving, sprinkle grated Parmesan and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked Thermidor in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. It can be frozen for up to 1 month, though the creamy sauce may change texture after thawing.

content.title: About
content.content: PediaSure is a specialized toddler nutritional drink formulated to support growth and development in children aged 1 to 3 years. The formula is enriched with vitamins, minerals, and proteins, providing balanced nutrition during periods of increased needs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: PediaSure is available in several flavors, including vanilla and chocolate.
The blend contains easily digestible milk and soy proteins.
Clinical studies have demonstrated its effectiveness in supporting weight gain in children with growth deficits.
It includes DHA and ARA, essential fatty acids for brain development.
PediaSure can be used as a supplement to regular meals under a healthcare professional’s guidance.

items.title: Supports growth
items.content: Balanced levels of protein, calcium, and vitamin D promote bone and muscle formation.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamins A, C and zinc help maintain the body’s defensive functions.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA contribute to the development of the nervous system and cognitive abilities.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Easily digestible carbohydrates provide a quick source of energy.

items.title: Improves nutritional status
items.content: Micronutrients such as iron and folic acid help prevent deficiency conditions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains milk protein; consult a physician if an allergy is known.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sugars are present, so intake should be limited for children at risk of dental caries.

items.title: Not a meal replacement
items.content: PediaSure is intended only as a supplement to a varied diet, not as a complete substitute.

items.title: Caloric excess
items.content: Overconsumption may lead to unwanted weight gain if total daily calories are not accounted for.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix 1 packet (≈30 g) with 200 ml of warm (not hot) water or milk. Recommended intake is 1–2 servings per day between meals, following pediatric guidance.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened packages in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use within 30 days and keep refrigerated.

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken turnover (also known as a hot pocket) is a ready‑to‑heat baked pastry that contains a filling of boiled or roasted chicken breast, vegetables and spices. The product is sealed in a moisture‑proof wrapper and designed for quick preparation in a microwave or conventional oven.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnovers were introduced in the United States in the 1970s as a convenient snack for busy people.
The filling often includes a small amount of cheese, which forms a golden crust when heated.
Chicken filling is typically made from skinless breast meat to keep the fat content low.
The product is commonly sold in single‑serve packs of 150‑200 g.
Some brands add whole vegetable pieces to boost nutritional value.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using skinless breast keeps the amount of saturated fat moderate.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is rich in vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Convenient and fast
items.content: A turnover can be ready in 2‑3 minutes, making it a practical quick‑meal option.

items.title: Balanced calories
items.content: One serving typically provides 250‑300 kcal, suitable for moderate diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made products often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Recipes may include dairy, gluten, or soy, which are common allergens.

items.title: Thermal safety
items.content: Insufficient heating can leave bacteria alive; heat the product to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Preservatives used to extend shelf life may not be suitable for individuals with sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the turnover in a microwave (≈ 1.5‑2 minutes on high) or in an oven (≈ 180 °C, 10‑12 minutes). Serve hot, optionally with fresh vegetables, herbs or a dipping sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package refrigerated at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 7‑10 days. If frozen, the product retains quality for up to 3 months.
